Net map: n1 = the whole top rail (y~168-176), from the top-left corner (56,169) across to the left end of resistor 3 (40 ohm): top lead of resistor 4 (10 ohm), top lead of I-DC 0 (T at (150,168)), top plate of capacitor 1 (T at (267,176)), left end of resistor 3. n2 = right end of resistor 3 -> top-right corner (405,179) -> down to the top of inductor 5 (0.125H). n3 = bottom plate of capacitor 1 -> straight down -> top (+) terminal of V-DC 2 (10V); nothing else on it. 0 = the whole bottom rail (y~331-336) plus GND 6: bottom-left corner (54,331), bottom lead of resistor 4, bottom lead of I-DC 0 (its lead runs down x=148, through the rail at (148,333) and on to the ground bars at y=357/364/367), bottom terminal of V-DC 2 (T at (268,335)), bottom of inductor 5 at the bottom-right corner (405,331).
Judgment calls: (a) the bootstrap had the bottom rail split into three nets (n4 on the left of the ground stub, 0 at the stub, n5 on the right). It is one wire: the rail is unbroken from (54,331) to (405,331) and the I-DC's ground lead simply passes through it at (148,333) on its way to the ground symbol below (there is a small thickening just above the rail but no clear dot). Reading that as a crossover would leave GND 6 reachable only through the current source, i.e. the source with no return path, and would split a plainly continuous straight wire - so it is a junction and the whole rail is "0". (b) Everything else is unambiguous: four clean T/corner meetings on the top rail and four on the bottom rail, all verified at 5-6x. (c) Terminal order: resistor 3 and the capacitor's plates are drawn horizontally/vertically respectively - resistor 3 indexed left then right; capacitor 1, V-DC 2, resistor 4, inductor 5 and I-DC 0 are all vertical and indexed top then bottom. V-DC 2 has "+" on the top half of its circle and I-DC 0's arrow points up, matching the top-first indexing; 2-terminal order does not affect any metric anyway. (d) No component was added, removed or re-classed.
